newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain says two German ETA suspects were hired guns.
newsitem.headline: Spain says two German ETA suspects were hired guns.

text.p: Two Germans suspected of being linked to the Basque separatist group ETA have been identified by German police as members of "radical" left-wing groups in that country, Spain's interior ministry said on Monday.

Renate Heike Schubert and Fritz Siedmund, both 33, were among four people who on Saturday fled from a Madrid safe house for ETA (Basque Homeland and Freedom) that was packed with weapons, a ministry spokesman told Reuters.

Interior Minister Jaime Mayor Oreja told a news conference on Monday that Schubert and Siedmund were mercenaries or hired guns used by ETA without any connection to the rebels' struggle for Basque independence.
"They are mercenaries paid for by ETA," he said. "Their link to ETA doesn't have any political motive."

The safe house was discovered on Saturday after an accidental explosion aroused neighbours' suspicions. The four fled the apartment complex after a neighbour knocked on their door to inquire and said he was going to alert police.
Police arrived minutes later and found arms, explosives and photographs of more than 400 public figures, including politicians, judges, military members, journalists and police.

The police have since located two more flats that they believed were also used as safe houses for a Madrid command unit of ETA. One had been rented by Siedmund and the other by Schubert last June and abandoned in early Februrary.

The minister said the possibility of links between German citizens and ETA, which has killed some 800 people since its independence drive in 1968, would be discussed in his next meeting with Germany's interior minister.

Spain has been investigating the possible collaboration of German nationals with the guerrilla group after a German woman was detained along with a senior ETA figure who was arrested in France in November 1996.
